questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed and shift to a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: When you brake, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, there may be a problem with your brakes.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: When the weather warms slightly, ice melts a little and becomes wet. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the maximum safe air leakage rate during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For double combination vehicles with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Before driving down a hill, shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as it goes down.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine with gears or a belt. The engine cools the compressor through its cooling system or with air cooling.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops between ____ psi.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should rise from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: Some air brake systems use alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system
Prevent people from breathing the air from the system

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you
Walk around the area first to check for obstacles

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area first to check for obstacles
questions.explanation: Before backing, walk around your vehicle to check the path and look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely only on them. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: What should you do about broken suspension parts?

options.text: Repair them, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired—it is dangerous. Coffee will not keep you safely awake.

questions.question: How should you view drivers talking to passengers in their vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not focus on the road. Be extra careful when driving near drivers who are distracted.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how should you brake?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before pressing hard on the pedal.
Press down hard on the brake pedal as hard as possible each time.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in an ABS vehicle as in a non-ABS vehicle. ABS automatically prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how can you make your vehicle more visible?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.

questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to help others see your vehicle.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high, which means there is a problem. Have a mechanic check the brakes.

questions.question: Is it good to keep space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: Yes, it gives you time to react to problems.
Only if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react safely if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What do drivers behind a slow-moving vehicle often do?
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone tailgates you, let them pass.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm others.
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm others.
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to hurt someone or damage their vehicle. Aggressive driving is different—it is selfish or pushy driving.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers and coffee do not speed up this process. You must wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.
